title: Natural moneymakers: the unemotional deal-makers who look like they're cheating
summary: Sam Parr introduces his newsletter and the idea of "natural moneymakers", entrepreneurs who make $100m to $1b through deal making and brokering. He says they are unemotional and logical about money. The essay is paywalled, so only the opening is available.

principles.text: Some founders are so good at making money it looks like cheating; Sam calls them natural moneymakers.
principles.quote: Some entrepreneurs are so violently good at making money it looks like cheating.

principles.text: Natural moneymakers tend to work in deal making, brokering and inserting themselves into situations, and they rarely build in public.
principles.quote: These people tend to be in roles that involve deal making, brokering, and inserting themselves into a situation. They rarely build in public.

principles.text: You can be a rich, successful founder without being a natural moneymaker; vision, risk and charisma are a different skill.
principles.quote: You can be successful and rich and still not be a natural money maker.

principles.text: Natural moneymakers treat business unemotionally and logically, even though they feel anxiety like everyone else.
principles.quote: Natural money makers have anxiety like everyone else. But they use emotions to make money.

principles.text: Passion and emotion help most founders succeed, but natural moneymakers are colder and more logical about money.
principles.quote: Being emotional and passionate helps founders succeed. Natural moneymakers are more cold about money. More logical.
